title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ashland, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ashland, MT
metaDescription: Ashland sits at the edge of the Northern Cheyenne Reservation in Rosebud County. A former engineer explains trust land, forest boundaries, and honest CBM-era value.
heroLead: Ashland sits where the Northern Cheyenne Reservation meets the Custer Gallatin National Forest, and both boundaries affect what you can actually do with a mineral interest here.
intro: Rosebud County's southern reaches, where Ashland sits, blend Northern Cheyenne tribal trust land, national forest land, and private fee ranchland in a way that makes a quick title check essential before any real conversation about value. This isn't a place where I'd guess at ownership status based on the county alone.

sections.heading: Trust Land and Forest Boundary Complications
paragraphs: If your family's interest traces to a Northern Cheyenne allotment, it may still be held in trust, requiring BIA approval to sell. If it sits adjacent to or within national forest boundaries, mineral development, if any is even possible, runs through additional federal land management rules on top of standard state regulation. Sorting out which of these applies to your specific tract is worth doing before you spend time comparing offers.

sections.heading: What's Actually Been Developed Nearby
paragraphs: Rosebud County has real coalbed methane history, mostly concentrated closer to Colstrip and the county's more developed northern areas. Near Ashland, that activity has historically been lighter, and I check current well records specifically rather than assume county-wide CBM development reaches this far south.

sections.heading: A Straightforward Path Forward
paragraphs: I'd confirm trust status first, check for any forest boundary complications second, and only then evaluate the underlying production or lease potential. For most Ashland-area owners, that turns up a modest interest with limited current development, and I'll give an honest range built on that reality rather than an inflated number that doesn't survive a title check.

faqs.question: Is my mineral interest near Ashland trust land or fee land?
faqs.answer: It could be either, given the Northern Cheyenne Reservation boundary running through this area. A title search at the Rosebud County Clerk and Recorder in Forsyth is the first step, followed by a BIA check if allotment history is confirmed.

faqs.question: Does national forest land near Ashland affect mineral development?
faqs.answer: It can. Federal forest land carries additional management rules on top of standard state oil and gas regulation, which is worth understanding if your tract sits near or within Custer Gallatin National Forest boundaries.

faqs.question: Is there active coalbed methane drilling near Ashland?
faqs.answer: Rosebud County's CBM activity has historically been more concentrated near Colstrip to the north. Development directly around Ashland has generally been lighter, so I check current records for the specific area.
